prompt: A peer writes 10 bytes as three separate sends (4, 4, 2) with small pauses. What can this single call return?
choices: Exactly 4, the size of the first send
0, because the data has not all arrived
explain: A stream socket has no message boundaries. `read` returns whatever is available, at least 1 byte if the peer is still connected. 0 means the peer closed. Loop until you have all the bytes you need.
